key_facts: serviceStadt Bremen program enables online applications for building permits and residence registration
Innovationscampus für Verwaltungsdigitalisierung launched to modernize citizen-facing digital services
Active e-Government network (e-Government – Made in Bremen) coordinates public-private digital transformation
Bremen leads national gigabit/fiber availability ranking due to city-state status
Regional Broadband Center actively expanding fiber rollout ahead of federal targets
smart-digital-mobil initiative coordinated across multiple Senate departments (Economy, Finance, Environment, Science)
WFB Bremen (Wirtschaftsförderung) runs regular multi-stakeholder workshops with industry, academia, and government
Active partnerships include University of Bremen, Governikus (city-owned e-government solutions provider), and bremenports (Smart Port strategy)
BITZ (Bremen Innovation and Technology Centre) hosts 80 technology companies adjacent to the University of Bremen
DFKI (German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence) has operated in Bremen for 30 years researching AI, robotics, and cyber-physical systems
ZARM (Center of Applied Space Technology and Microgravity) and aerospace cluster anchor Bremen's position in space/aviation innovation alongside Airbus and OHB
Official tourism Instagram (@visit.bremen) has 62K followers and 1,655 posts with active branded hashtag campaigns (#visitbremen, #enjoybremen)
WFB Bremen runs a dedicated economic/tech channel spotlighting local startups and companies, separate from general city channels
Official city X/Twitter account (@bremen_de) was discontinued, redirecting followers to Instagram and TikTok — reflecting a deliberate platform-strategy shift toward visual/short-form channels
